product.category: AI voice agent platform for call centers

market.sizeHint: [inferred] Large market; call center industry is multi-billion dollar globally, but no specific size given.

risks.text: Dependence on third-party LLMs and speech APIs could reduce defensibility if competitors use same underlying models.
No explicit mention of proprietary data or workflow lock-in; risk of being a thin wrapper.
Competitive market with many AI voice agent startups; differentiation may erode over time.

subScores.label: Team
subScores.rationale: Strong founder-market fit with relevant big-tech experience in AI, speech, and ads. Technical depth is high. No confirmed prior exits for most founders, but Todd Li is a repeat founder.

subScores.label: Defensibility
subScores.rationale: No clear proprietary data or workflow lock-in mentioned. Likely relies on third-party LLMs and speech APIs, making it a potential thin wrapper. Switching costs may be low for customers.

subScores.label: Product
subScores.rationale: AI-native agent that takes actions end-to-end (voice calls). Self-serve onboarding likely for SMBs. One-liner is clear and concise.

subScores.label: Market & Why-Now
subScores.rationale: Specific vertical (call centers) with large addressable market. Why-now is strong due to LLM cost collapse and speech AI advances. Competitors exist but wedge is speed/growth.

subScores.label: Traction / Freshness
subScores.rationale: Reported 40 million monthly calls and described as fastest-growing. Signal is recent and strong, though source is a press article.

scoreRationale: Retell AI has a strong team and product with clear traction in a large market, but defensibility is a concern due to potential reliance on third-party models. Overall a promising investment candidate.
